solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Impostor? Nonsense

definitions.meaning: a fraud or sham person who pretends to be what they are not

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a deceiving fraud and the claptrap such a fraud talks, so both senses fit.

clue.text: Drunken bum's ardour causing offence

indicators.note: a drunken thing staggers about, so the letters of the word bum are jumbled

parts.note: the word bum, its possessive adding no letter
ardour, a passion, can be a rage

explanation.surface: A drunk tramp's passionate behaviour gives offence to others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'causing' is only a link before the definition; 'bum' here is a tramp, as in the surface, but only its letters matter.
explanation.definitionFit: To take umbrage is to take offence, so the noun is a synonym for offence.

clue.text: Carrot bachelor covered with cheese

indicators.note: the bachelor's letter is wrapped up inside the cheese, as if covered by it

parts.note: Brie is a soft French cheese

explanation.surface: A carrot for a single man, smothered in cheese, like a recipe.
explanation.definitionFit: A carrot is an inducement, and an inducement offered to sway someone corruptly is a sweetener of that kind.

clue.text: Novelist suppressing joke — it's fruity

indicators.note: the novelist holds the joke down inside his name, keeping it in

parts.note: Graham Greene was an English novelist
a gag is a joke

explanation.surface: A writer holds back a joke because it is rather risqué.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's fruity' looks like a comment on a racy joke but defines a fruit, a green plum.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a kind of green plum, so something fruity in the literal sense.

clue.text: Disease, nasty-sounding — pets affected

indicators.note: the hyphenated tag says a word for nasty is to be heard, not spelt

parts.note: nasty means foul

indicators.note: affected here means altered, so the letters of pets are rearranged

explanation.surface: A disease that sounds horrible has struck the household pets.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an avian illness, a highly infectious viral sickness of poultry.

clue.text: Following suit, mostly to impress a new group of admirers

indicators.note: to impress is to press something into another, so the letters go inside

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

indicators.note: mostly means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: clubs is one of the four suits in cards

explanation.surface: Copying others, someone tries to win over a fresh set of supporters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Following suit' reads as copying others, but each word gives its own piece; 'to impress' pushes A and N into the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A society of devoted followers of a star or team is exactly a body of admirers.

clue.text: Bet salary on first of runners

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed after, below the other piece

parts.note: a wage is regular pay, a salary

indicators.note: first of means take the opening letter of runners

explanation.surface: A punter stakes their pay on the leading horse in a race.
explanation.definitionFit: A stake placed on an outcome is a gamble, the same thing as a bet.

clue.text: In favour of writer exposing outlaw

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
a scribe is a writer or copyist

explanation.surface: Someone supporting a writer who exposes a fugitive criminal.
explanation.definitionFit: To ban or forbid formally is to outlaw, used here as a verb.

clue.text: Influential in workshop, ignoring right line

indicators.note: ignoring the right letter means it is dropped, with the line letter put in its place

parts.note: a seminar is a discussion class or workshop

explanation.surface: Someone influential at a training session who disregards the correct procedure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word between definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Seminal work is highly influential, shaping much that follows.

clue.text: Honeymoon suite for them — grand bedroom, I suspect

indicators.note: suspect as an adjective means dubious, so the letters are treated as unreliable and reordered

explanation.surface: A guess that the luxurious bedroom is meant for a newly married couple.
explanation.definitionFit: The couple at a wedding are the people a honeymoon suite is booked for.

clue.text: Mate ringing a seabird is taking protective interest

indicators.note: ringing means encircling, so the friend goes round the other pieces

parts.note: a pal is a mate, a friend
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A friend fitting a ring to a seabird's leg shows care for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Fatherly concern is a protective interest, as a father has in a child.

clue.text: French dramatist elected to enter competition

indicators.note: to enter means go inside, so the elected word sits within the competition word

parts.note: a race is a competition
in means elected, as a party voted in

explanation.surface: A French playwright has been chosen to take part in a contest.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean Racine was a seventeenth-century French tragedian, author of Phèdre.

clue.text: Nothing about English version in US state

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for nothing goes round the other letters

parts.note: nada is Spanish-derived slang for nothing
V is the abbreviation for version, as in Bible versions

explanation.surface: No mention of an English edition in an American state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a western state of America, home to Las Vegas.

clue.text: Suddenly, everyone agreed about carbon

parts.note: all means everyone

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for agreed surrounds the carbon symbol

parts.note: at one means in agreement
C is the chemical symbol for carbon

explanation.surface: Everybody abruptly comes to agreement on carbon emissions.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom meaning abruptly, all in one moment, so a synonym for suddenly.

clue.text: Work in vile Parisian prison

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the work word goes within the vile word

parts.note: base means vile, low
to till is to work the soil

explanation.surface: Labour in a horrible jail in Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bastille was the Paris fortress jail stormed in 1789 at the start of the Revolution.

clue.text: Political leaders ordered means test

indicators.note: ordered means arranged afresh, so these letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Government heads have demanded a test of people's income.
explanation.definitionFit: Senior politicians of standing are described as statespeople, i.e. political leaders.

clue.text: A female, silver-tongued and wealthy

parts.note: silver-tongued means eloquent, fluent in speech

explanation.surface: A woman who is persuasive in speech and rich too.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with plenty of money is rich, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Perplex loud clumsy person

parts.note: F, forte, is the musical abbreviation for loud
a lummox is a clumsy, stupid person

explanation.surface: Bewilder a noisy oaf.
explanation.definitionFit: To baffle or confuse someone completely, a synonym of perplex.

clue.text: Vandalised paintings mounted in front of hut

indicators.note: in front of means placed before the next piece
in a down clue, mounted means turned upwards, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: art covers paintings
a shed is a hut

explanation.surface: Pictures hung outside a shed have been defaced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mounted' suggests framing pictures, but in a down answer it signals reading upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To trash a place is to wreck it wantonly, i.e. to vandalise it.

clue.text: Pop out after beer in Syrian city

indicators.note: after means this piece comes behind the beer

parts.note: ale is beer

indicators.note: out means wrong or disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone nips out for a drink in a city in Syria.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pop out' reads as nipping out, but 'out' is the anagram signal; 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Aleppo is a major ancient city in northern Syria.

clue.text: Crack in planter's recent

parts.note: a plant pot is a planter, and with the possessive gives pot's
hot means very recent, as in hot news

explanation.surface: A fissure in a gardener's latest container.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word; the 's of planter's supplies an S here.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a crack at something is taking a casual attempt, like a random shot.

clue.text: Foremost of players to speak in golf club

indicators.note: foremost of means take the leading letter of players

parts.note: to utter is to speak

explanation.surface: The leading players get to talk at a golf club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the club used on the green for rolling the ball into the hole.

clue.text: Fire damaged rear of boat, resulting in this?

definitions.text: Fire damaged rear of boat, resulting in this?

indicators.note: damaged means broken up, so the letters of fire are rearranged
rear of means take the last letter of boat

explanation.surface: A blaze wrecked the back of a vessel, which then needed repairs.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat damaged by fire would need a refit, an overhaul and re-equipping.

clue.text: Story one cadet concocted

indicators.note: concocted means made up, so the letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A tale invented by a military trainee.
explanation.definitionFit: A short amusing account of a real incident is a type of story.

clue.text: Old-fashioned old man penning note

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, so the father word holds the note

parts.note: old man is slang for father, dad
te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: An outdated father writing a short note.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that has gone out of style is out of date, so old-fashioned.

clue.text: Guy at No.9, best player on pitch?

definitions.meaning: a man at the wedding of the couple at 9 across, a match being a marriage
the award for the outstanding player in a game

explanation.definitionFit: A match is a marriage and also a game, so the phrase suits a guy at the wedding as well as the star player.

clue.text: In power replacing Liberal? Vote received makes this likely

indicators.note: received means taken in, so the vote letter goes inside
replacing means the power letter stands where the Liberal letter was

parts.note: a party that is in has been elected
X is the cross marking a vote on a ballot paper

explanation.surface: A political musing that a vote will probably put someone in power in place of the Liberals.
explanation.walkthrough: In = ELECTED; P replacing L gives EPECTED, which receives X; 'makes this' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: What is anticipated as probable is expected, so likely is a fair synonym.

clue.text: Untidy, dancing in state of undress

indicators.note: dancing means moving about, so the letters of untidy are rearranged

explanation.surface: A messy dancer ends up with no clothes on.
explanation.definitionFit: Being naked is having no clothes, the condition of being undressed.
